## tfskel completion zsh

Generate the autocompletion script for zsh

### Synopsis

Generate the autocompletion script for the zsh shell.

If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need
to enable it.  You can execute the following once:

	echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit" >> ~/.zshrc

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(tfskel completion zsh)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	tfskel completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_tfskel"

#### macOS:

	tfskel completion zsh > $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/_tfskel

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.


```
tfskel completion zsh [flags]
```

### Options

```
  -h, --help              help for zsh
      --no-descriptions   disable completion descriptions
```

### Options inherited from parent commands

```
  -c, --config string   config file (default is .tfskel.yaml in current directory)
      --dry-run         show what would happen without writing files
      --no-color        disable colored output (respects NO_COLOR and FORCE_COLOR env vars)
  -v, --verbose         enable verbose output
```
